title: Composition of pro-etale module inverse images with canonical constant coefficients
statement:
Let $g:Z\to X$ and $f:X\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale sites and universe conventions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with constant ring sheaves $\Lambda_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and their module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h=f,g,f\circ g$ let $h^*$ and $h_*$ be the module inverse image and direct image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], using precisely its canonical constant-section map $c^h_\Lambda$. There is a natural isomorphism of functors
$$(f\circ g)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*f^*:\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_Z).$$
It is the canonical comparison of left adjoints to the direct-image identification $(f\circ g)_*\cong f_*g_*$ induced on each object $V\to Y$ by $Z\times_X(X\times_YV)\cong Z\times_YV$, with the module actions given by the specified constant-section maps.

proof.text: Put $h=f\circ g$ and use the base-change functors $u_a$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $V\to Y$, the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $q_V:u_gu_f(V)=Z\times_X(X\times_YV)\xrightarrow{\sim}Z\times_YV=u_h(V)$. Its components are the projection to $Z$ and the projection to $V$; its inverse has components the projection to $Z$ and the pair consisting of $g$ after that projection and the projection to $V$. Both composites have the identity projections, hence are identities. For an arrow $V'\to V$, both paths in the naturality square have the same projections to $Z$ and $V$, so are equal. Thus for any abelian sheaf $H$ on $Z$, restriction along $q_V$ defines a natural isomorphism $d_H:h_*H\to f_*g_*H$ on underlying abelian sheaves. It commutes with restrictions in $V$ by the naturality just checked, and with maps in $H$ by their presheaf naturality; its inverse is restriction along $q_V^{-1}$.

proof.text:
Use the same restriction formula on the ring sheaf $\Lambda_Z$, obtaining a ring-sheaf isomorphism $d_{\Lambda_Z}:h_*\Lambda_Z\to f_*g_*\Lambda_Z$. Write $\rho^a:\Lambda_{\mathrm{target}(a)}\to a_*\Lambda_{\mathrm{source}(a)}$ for the maps defined in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then
$$d_{\Lambda_Z}\circ\rho^h=f_*(\rho^g)\circ\rho^f.$$
Indeed, precompose both sides with the constant-presheaf sheafification map to $\Lambda_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. At every $V$ they send $\lambda\in\Lambda$ to the constant section $\lambda$ on $u_gu_f(V)$: $\rho^f$ and $\rho^g$ do so by definition, and restriction along $q_V$ preserves that constant section by naturality of the constant-presheaf map. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] proves equality on all of $\Lambda_Y$, not merely on its global constant sections.

proof.text:
For a $\Lambda_Z$-module sheaf $H$, $s\in\Lambda_Y(V)$ and $m\in H(u_h(V))$, semilinearity of restriction in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives
$$H(q_V)(\rho^h_V(s)m)=\Lambda_Z(q_V)(\rho^h_V(s))\,H(q_V)(m)=\rho^g_{u_f(V)}(\rho^f_V(s))\,H(q_V)(m).$$
The second equality is step 2. By the direct-image action formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the last expression is precisely $s$ acting on $d_{H,V}(m)$ in $f_*g_*H(V)$. Hence $d_H$ is $\Lambda_Y$-linear. Its inverse is linear too: for $n=d_H(m)$ the displayed equality reads $d_H^{-1}(sn)=s\,d_H^{-1}(n)$. The naturality from step 1 therefore gives the required natural isomorphism $d:h_*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*g_*$ on module categories, with exactly the prescribed actions.

source.place: Tag 03D8, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules: linearity of the direct-image comparison

proof.text: For each $a=f,g,h$, the inverse image in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] preserves finite limits and is left adjoint to the sectionwise direct image. Its ring map $c^a_\Lambda$ is, by that definition, adjoint to the very $\rho^a$ used above. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] with $R=\Lambda_{\mathrm{target}(a)}$, $S=\Lambda_{\mathrm{source}(a)}$ and $c=c^a_\Lambda$. Its tensor-formula pullback is the stated $a^*$ (commuting the two tensor factors over the commutative ring is the balanced map $x\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes x$, inverse to the same switch), and its pushforward action is through $\rho^a$. Thus $a^*\dashv a_*$. The composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives $g^*f^*\dashv f_*g_*$; also $h^*\dashv h_*$. All sites and module categories are in the compatible universes specified in the item, so the cited adjunctions apply without a size change.

proof.text: Apply the bijection on natural isomorphisms in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to $L_1=h^*$, $R_1=h_*$ and $L_2=g^*f^*$, $R_2=f_*g_*$. The isomorphism $d:R_1\xrightarrow{\sim}R_2$ of step 3 has a unique conjugate $t:L_2\xrightarrow{\sim}L_1$. Set $b=t^{-1}:h^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*f^*$. This proves the claimed natural isomorphism. Its inverse $b^{-1}$ is conjugate to $d$, equivalently $b$ is conjugate to $d^{-1}$ under the reversed adjunctions. Consequently it is exactly the canonical comparison of left adjoints attached to the fibre-product direct-image identification of the statement, rather than a choice of an unrelated isomorphism.
